PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality franchise in a margin-compression cycle, but the quantitative trajectory is deteriorating faster than the valuation compensates. Three consecutive quarters of declining EPS ($1.95→$1.78→$1.63) and operating margin compression (26.2%→21.6%) are the dominant signal. The PE at 23.1x is near the low end of its 365-day range (21.7x–26.3x) but not cheap in absolute terms — earnings yield (4.3%) now sits below the 10-year Treasury yield (4.54%), a meaningful headwind for a defensive equity. The market has pass passively repriced the PE compression (~7%) is modest relative to the operating margin decline (~460bps). The near-term outlook is further clouded by $400M tariff costs in FY2026 and a $1B oil cost headwind in FY2027, a restructuring program with 7,000 job cuts introducing execution risk, and a CEO transition. While the franchise's structural moat is intact and oil's -27% decline could eventually provide input cost relief, this is not yet visible in the fundamentals. The sequential OCF decline ($5.41B→$4.04B, -25.3%) raises questions about dividend coverage sustainability. The Thorne acquisition ($3.8B) and AI productivity investments are long-term positives but do not address the near-term margin squeeze. I exclude the Q4 FY2026 results cited in the qualitative report as they were not public as of the 2026-07-10 decision date (reported July 29, 2026).
key_factors: Three consecutive quarters of declining EPS: $1.95 (Q1 FY26) → $1.78 (Q2 FY26) → $1.63 (Q3 FY26), cumulative -16.4% sequential decline
Operating margin compression from ~26.2% (Q1) to ~21.6% (Q3), driven by tariff and input cost headwinds
PE of 23.1x near low end of 365-day range (21.7x–26.3x) but earnings yield (4.3%) below 10-year Treasury yield (4.54%)
PE compression of ~7% (from 24.9x to 23.1x) is modest relative to ~460bps operating margin decline, suggesting market has not fully repriced deterioration
Sequential OCF decline from $5.41B (Q1) to $4.04B (Q3), -25.3% cumulative, raising dividend coverage questions
$400M after-tax tariff costs in FY2026 and ~$1B after-tax oil cost headwind expected for FY2027 (Iran conflict, crude from ~$60 to ~$100/bbl)
Restructuring program targeting up to 7,000 non-manufacturing job cuts with CEO transition adding execution uncertainty
YoY revenue growth of +7.4% and EPS growth of +5.8% demonstrate underlying franchise still expanding, but deceleration rate is concerning
Balance sheet stable: equity grew +6.4% over five quarters to $54.73B, ROE 29.7%, debt-to-equity ~1.35x
Oil's -27% decline (WTI from ~$100 to $73/bbl) could provide input cost relief with a lag, but not yet visible in fundamentals
